live_frontier_title: cutoff-center analytic remainder / one-step activity closure
current_determination: The global-center problem for the preferred single translated heat-kernel blocker is structurally closed by an explicit cutoff-logarithm construction. Anchor each coarse link to a canonical straight fine path U0; form relative endpoint loops R_j=U0^{-1}U_j; apply a smooth conjugation- and inversion-invariant cutoff times the local logarithm, phi(R)=chi(R)log R, with chi supported strictly inside the logarithm chart; and define C_e(U)=U0 exp(sum_j w_j phi(R_j)). This center is globally smooth, endpoint-gauge covariant, exactly orientation covariant, reflection covariant under an equivariant path assignment, and half-space local for reflection-aligned path families. On the regular small-field chart chi=1, so the center is complex analytic and has jet C_e(exp(gA))=exp(g(QA)_e+O(g^2)). The YM-R17 no-global-mean obstruction is avoided because the center is not permutation symmetric among all paths; the distinguished straight path is geometrically covariant rather than physically symmetry-breaking. The remaining UV obligation is quantitative analytic control of the O(g) nonlinear center/heat-kernel remainder through the CMP116 localization and activity bound.
major_new_results: An explicit global center exists without a canonical symmetric group mean: C_e=U0 exp(sum_j w_j phi(U0^{-1}U_j)) with phi=chi log on a regular chart and zero outside the cutoff support.
Gauge covariance follows because relative loops transform by conjugation at the endpoint; orientation covariance follows from phi(R^{-1})=-phi(R).

Reflection covariance and positive-half-space locality are obtained by choosing the path family equivariantly and keeping positive-link paths inside the positive half-space, with separate boundary treatment at the reflection plane.
On the regular chart the cutoff is identically one, so the center is holomorphic there and its linear jet is exactly the weighted path average Q.

A canonical straight fine path can serve as the distinguished anchor without destroying hypercubic covariance; the topology obstruction is avoided by giving up permutation symmetry of all paths, not by giving up lattice symmetry.
The single translated heat-kernel blocker can therefore simultaneously have exact normalization, gauge/RP covariance, the Bałaban Gaussian Hessian, and a globally defined center.
negative_results: No global holomorphic center is claimed; the cutoff extension is only smooth outside the regular chart, and large-field sectors must remain in exact nonperturbative bookkeeping.
The construction does not by itself prove Bałaban polymer-norm closure or the continuum theory.
Do not return to the path-mixture heat kernel unless an additional small-cumulant theorem is supplied; the single-center kernel is the preferred UV object.
live_obligations: Bound the nonlinear jet C_e(exp(gA)) exp(-gQA) on the fixed complex regular tube, including first and higher derivatives with constants uniform in RG scale.

Combine those bounds with compact-group small-time heat-kernel asymptotics for t_k=g_k^2/a to isolate the principal Gaussian and obtain a raw local factor 1+O(g_k) (or exp of an O(g_k) analytic functional).
Extract vacuum and Wilson-action components and identify the complementary local jet.
Insert the resulting local perturbation into the CMP116 product-Gaussian/random-walk localization chain and prove a Lemma-3-type exponentially localized H_soft(Z) bound.
Keep RP custody at the exact kernel level; do not truncate the blocked measure to the local jet.
